author: Phipps, 1774
summary: 몸 전체가 흰 갈매기로, 몸 크기는 괭이갈매기보다 작은 편이다. 유라시아 대륙과 북아메리카의 북극권에 분포한다.

points.en: black-based bill with a yellow tip
black spots scattered on back and upperwing

art.subject: Ivory Gull (Pagophila eburnea), first-winter: plumage white, with small black spots scattered over the back and wing coverts and black tips to the primaries, secondaries and tail feathers; face dusky grey around the bill and eye, giving black lores. Bill dark grey-black with a yellowish tip; dark eye; short black legs.
art.scene: Korean east coast in winter, snow on dark rocks beside a grey sea; no people, buildings or text
views: first-winter, side view standing: white body, black spots on the back and wing coverts, black tips to the primaries, dusky face with black lores, dark bill with a yellowish tip, short black legs
first-winter in flight, seen from above: white wings with neat black spots across the coverts and black tips to the flight feathers and tail
adult, side view standing: pure white all over without spots, bill bluish grey at the base and yellow at the tip, short black legs
art.build: Small, compact gull, smaller than the Black-tailed Gull, plump and pigeon-like with a rounded head, short neck and full chest. Bill short and stout, shorter than the head. Legs very short and black, so it sits low and walks like a pigeon. At rest the long wings project well beyond the tail. Wings broad-based and fairly pointed; tail square. The adult is entirely pure white with no black in the plumage, its bill greyish at the base and yellow at the tip.
avoid: Do not give it a grey back or grey wings; unlike other gulls it has no grey in the plumage.
Do not paint solid black wingtips like a Black-tailed Gull; young birds have only small black spots and tips.
Do not paint long, yellow or pink legs; the legs are short and black.
Do not put black spots on an adult; adults are pure white.
